title: Sicilian Defense: Alapin Variation
line: White gets ready for a second center pawn; Black hits back at once, and the queen can come out early.

steps.text: Here White pushes the pawn on c2 one square, to back up a pawn on d4 next.
Strike at once: push the pawn on d7 two squares and attack the pawn on e4.

also.g8f6: That is the other main answer, and it is just as sound. This lesson goes on with the pawn.

steps.text: A knight usually comes out to chase a queen like this. Tap the white pawn that stands on the knight's square.
steps.after: The pawn holds the knight's square, so no knight can come from there to chase your queen.

steps.text: Bring the bishop out to pin the knight that guards d4.
Push the pawn on e7 one square, so your other bishop can come out.
Bring the other knight out. Your queen, this knight and your pawn all hit the pawn on d4.
steps.after: White's pawn asks your bishop to decide. The pawn on d4 is still attacked three times.

summary: Against the Alapin, Black strikes at the center at once, and the queen is safe because no knight can chase her.
